Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "our college film society meets every wednesday in the media room, which is on the second floor of the library. we watch one film at each meeting, and the person who picks it changes from week to week. after the screening, we talk about what worked and what did not, though the discussion can get a little long if people have different opinions about the ending. membership is open to students from any department, and there is no fee to attend.

for next month, we have booked the small auditorium for a screening of the 1975 film Barry Lyndon on november 14. the doors open at 6:30 p.m., and the film begins at 7. the auditorium has more seats than our usual room, so we are hoping people will bring a friend if they want to. we usually post the film choice and meeting details on the society's noticeboard and group page, but sometimes the post goes up only a few days before the meeting. i think Barry Lyndon is perhaps a slightly unusual choice for us because it is longer than most of the films we have shown this term. still, the screening will be followed by our regular discussion, and students can leave whenever they need to.", "output": "Our college film society meets every Wednesday in the media room on the second floor of the library. We watch one film at each meeting, with a different person choosing the film each week. After the screening, we talk about what worked and what didn’t. The discussion can run a little long when people have different opinions about the ending. Membership is open to students from any department, and there is no fee to attend.

Next month, we have booked the small auditorium for a screening of the 1975 film Barry Lyndon on November 14. The doors open at 6:30 p.m., and the film begins at 7. The auditorium has more seats than our usual room, so we hope people will bring a friend if they wish. We usually post the film choice and meeting details on the society’s noticeboard and group page, though sometimes the post goes up only a few days before the meeting. I think Barry Lyndon may be a slightly unusual choice for us because it is longer than most of the films we have shown this term. The screening will be followed by our regular discussion, and students can leave whenever they need to."}]
